_about: Batch B10a writer (structured outputs, determinism, low-precision formats, structure_output/ and linear.py code pages). Format terms (fp8, e4m3, fp4, ue8m0, mxfp4, mxfp8, block-scaling, quantization, scale-factor) are in b2.json, core.json and platform.json; do not redefine them here.

xgrammar.short: An open-source library that compiles a grammar (JSON schema, regex or EBNF) for a tokenizer, and then gives the set of allowed next tokens. DeepInfer installs it from pip.
xgrammar.long: DeepInfer calls only its GrammarCompiler, GrammarMatcher and bitmask helpers ({{cite deepinfer/structure_output/compiler.py:6-7}}, {{cite deepinfer/structure_output/matcher.py:12-14}}).

grammar-matcher.short: An object that follows one request through its grammar. It accepts each new token, tells which tokens may come next, and can roll back a few tokens. In DeepInfer it is XGrammarMatcher.
grammar-matcher.long: Defined at {{cite deepinfer/structure_output/matcher.py:58}}. Its rollback depth is DEEPINFER_USE_NEXTN_DECODE + 2 ({{cite deepinfer/structure_output/matcher.py:20}}).

token-bitmask.short: One bit per vocabulary token, packed 32 to an int32 word. Bit 1 means the grammar allows the token. A kernel sets the logit of every token with bit 0 to minus infinity.

json-schema.short: A JSON document that describes the allowed shape of other JSON: the keys, their types and the allowed values. DeepInfer passes it with schema_type "json".

regular-expression.short: A short pattern that describes a set of strings, for example [A-Z]{2}-[0-9]{3}. DeepInfer passes it with schema_type "regex".

ebnf.short: Extended Backus-Naur form: a notation for grammars with rules such as root ::= "yes" | "no". DeepInfer passes it with schema_type "ebnf".

trigger-tokens.short: An optional token sequence in so_args (trigger_token_ids). Generation is free until the full sequence appears; after it, the grammar applies.

bound-token.short: An optional token id in so_args (bound_token_id). After this token, the request must write the trigger tokens next, one by one, and then follow the grammar.

kmp.short: Knuth-Morris-Pratt: a way to find a pattern in a stream. A precomputed failure table tells how much of the pattern still matches after a mismatch, so no token is read twice.

so-status.short: The structured-output state of a sequence in C++: 0 not started, 1 at the boundary (last prompt chunk), 2 running, -1 aborted. A request without a grammar keeps 0.

thread-pool.short: A fixed group of worker threads that run submitted tasks. Each submit returns a future; the caller checks the future later for the result.

batch-invariance.short: A request gives bit-identical results, whatever other requests share its batch. DeepInfer turns it on with DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1 (NVIDIA only).

determinism.short: The same inputs give the same outputs, bit for bit, on every run. In DeepInfer, deterministic sampling needs DEEPINFER_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, DEEPINFER_ENABLE_MTP_VARLEN=0 and a fixed seq_seed.

reduction-order.short: The order in which a kernel adds many numbers. Each addition rounds, so a different order can give a different last bit.

kl-divergence.short: A measure of how much one probability distribution differs from another. It is 0 only when they are equal. DeepInfer's KL test uses an estimate of it to compare two sets of logprobs.

round-to-nearest-even.term: round to nearest, ties to even
round-to-nearest-even.short: The default float rounding rule: take the nearest representable value; when a value is exactly halfway, take the one whose last mantissa bit is 0.

saturation.short: A conversion rule for values above the largest code: store the largest code (for example 448 in E4M3) instead of infinity or NaN.

subnormal.short: A small floating-point value with exponent field 0: 0.mantissa × 2^(1 − bias). Subnormals fill the gap between 0 and the smallest normal value.

amax.short: The largest absolute value in a group of numbers. A quantize kernel divides it by the format maximum to choose the scale of the group.

per-token-quantization.short: Each token row of an activation gets its own scales, here one UE8M0 scale per 32 values. The kernel computes them at run time from the row (dynamic scaling).

qat.short: Quantization-aware training: the model trains with the low-precision rounding in the loop, so its weights already fit the small format.
